phrases.translation: The command of Allah is at hand, so do not hasten it.
phrases.explanation: God announces that His command has drawn so close and is so certain to arrive that it is spoken of as having already come. Early interpreters differed over what this command refers to: many said it means the Hour of Judgment and the decreed punishment that the Meccan polytheists mockingly demanded to see right away, while others said it refers to God’s revealed laws, obligations, and rulings.

phrases.translation: Glorified and Exalted is He above what they associate ˹with Him in worship˺
phrases.explanation: God declares His absolute perfection and transcendence far above the idols, partners, and false deities that the polytheists associate with Him in worship. Because He alone commands creation and brings about the Hour without partner or rival, nothing they set up beside Him has any share in divinity.

phrases.translation: He sends down the angels with revelation by His command to whoever He wills of His servants,
phrases.explanation: God sends down the angels bearing the life-giving spirit of revelation and scripture by His command upon whichever of His chosen servants He selects for prophethood. Just as rain revives dead earth, divine revelation brings dead hearts to life by making truth clear and exposing falsehood.

phrases.translation: ˹stating:˺ “Warn ˹humanity˺ that there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Me, so be mindful of Me ˹alone˺.”
phrases.explanation: The core message entrusted to every prophet across history is to warn humanity against polytheism and proclaim that there is no deity worthy of worship except God alone. People are therefore commanded to fear God’s punishment by obeying His commands and dedicating their worship exclusively to Him.

phrases.translation: He created the heavens and the earth for a purpose.
phrases.explanation: Among the clearest proofs of God’s oneness and sole lordship is that He alone created the heavens and the earth with truth, wisdom, and justice rather than in vain. No idol, angel, or alleged partner assisted Him in bringing the universe into existence out of nothing or governing its order.

phrases.translation: Exalted is He above what they associate with Him ˹in worship˺
phrases.explanation: God is exalted far above the false gods and equals that the idolaters associate with Him. Only the One Who originates the heavens and the earth out of nothing by His power deserves to be worshipped, whereas helpless creatures can never be partners to the Creator.

phrases.translation: He created humans from a sperm-drop, then—behold!—they openly challenge ˹Him˺
phrases.explanation: God reminds humanity of its humble beginning from a lowly drop of fluid that He shaped in stages within the womb and brought forth as a living, thinking person. Yet once grown and strong, the ungrateful human being forgets the Creator Who formed him from nothing and openly disputes with his Lord, denying resurrection and worshipping powerless idols.

phrases.translation: And He created the cattle for you as a source of warmth, food, and ˹many other˺ benefits
phrases.explanation: Among God’s favors and proofs of His lordship is that He created livestock such as camels, cattle, and sheep and subjected them to human beings. From their wool, fur, and hair people make warm clothing and coverings to ward off the cold, while also enjoying their milk, offspring, riding use, and lawful meat.

phrases.translation: They are also pleasing to you when you bring them home and when you take them out to graze
phrases.explanation: Beyond physical survival, these herds and flocks bring beauty, pride, and visual delight to their owners in daily life. People enjoy watching them return with full udders to their resting folds in the evening and seeing them driven out to their pastures to graze in the morning.

phrases.translation: And they carry your loads to ˹distant˺ lands which you could not otherwise reach without great hardship.
phrases.explanation: Camels and pack animals also carry heavy loads of goods, baggage, and provisions across long distances to lands, such as Mecca and distant trading cities, that travelers could never reach by their own strength without exhausting their bodies and pushing themselves to the limit of endurance.

phrases.translation: Surely your Lord is Ever Gracious, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: In providing these strong beasts of burden to carry heavy loads that would otherwise exhaust and overwhelm human beings, your Lord shows how gentle, compassionate, and merciful He is toward His servants, sparing them unbearable hardship in their daily livelihood and long journeys across the earth, and calling them to thank Him alone.

phrases.translation: ˹He also created˺ horses, mules, and donkeys for your transportation and adornment.
phrases.explanation: God also created horses, mules, and donkeys so that people may ride them in travel and warfare and take pride in them as a source of beauty and worldly grace. Some early scholars noted that mentioning riding here, unlike the mention of eating regarding cattle, indicated a distinction in their primary use.

phrases.translation: And He creates what you do not know
phrases.explanation: Beyond the animals familiar to human beings, God continually creates other creatures, marvels, and forms of life and provision of which people have no knowledge in this world. His creative power is never exhausted and extends far beyond what human eyes have seen or minds have conceived.

phrases.translation: It is upon Allah ˹alone˺ to ˹clearly˺ show the Straight Way. Other ways are deviant.
phrases.explanation: God has taken it upon Himself by His grace to make clear to humanity the straight, direct path of truth, which is Islam, so that whoever follows it reaches safety. Alongside that straight road are crooked, deviating paths of error and false religions that turn away from truth and lead to ruin.

phrases.translation: Had He willed, He would have easily imposed guidance upon all of you
phrases.explanation: Had God willed to compel all human beings onto faith, He could easily have guided everyone to the truth as a single community without exception. Instead, in His wisdom He clarified the straight path from the crooked roads and left people accountable for the way they choose.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who sends down rain from the sky, from which you drink and by which plants grow for your cattle to graze
phrases.explanation: The same Lord Who created these animals for your benefit also sends down rain from the clouds, providing fresh, sweet water for human beings to drink and bringing forth lush pastures, plants, and trees in which you let your livestock graze freely across the land.

phrases.translation: With it He produces for you ˹various˺ crops, olives, palm trees, grapevines, and every type of fruit.
phrases.explanation: By means of that single rainwater sent down from the sky, God causes the earth to produce diverse staple crops of grain alongside olive trees, date palms, grapevines, and every other variety of fruit to nourish and delight humanity with wholesome food, oil, and drink as a favor from their Creator.

phrases.translation: Surely in this is a sign for those who reflect
phrases.explanation: Bringing forth so many different colors, shapes, flavors, and kinds of fruit from the very same rainwater and soil is a clear sign and decisive proof of God’s oneness and creative power for people who reflect upon His creation and take heed of His countless blessings.

phrases.translation: And He has subjected for your benefit the day and the night, the sun and the moon. And the stars have been subjected by His command.
phrases.explanation: God has also subjected the alternating night and day for human rest and work, and subjected the sun and the moon to mark seasons, months, and years while ripening crops. Likewise, the stars move in their courses by His command so travelers can find direction on land and sea.

phrases.translation: Surely in this are signs for those who understand
phrases.explanation: In the precise, unfailing order of these mighty heavenly bodies serving human needs day after day and season after season are unmistakable signs of the Creator’s power, wisdom, and sole divinity for people who use their reason, comprehend God’s proofs, and take admonition to heart.

phrases.translation: And ˹He subjected˺ for you whatever He has created on earth of varying colours.
phrases.explanation: God has likewise subjected for human benefit all the diverse things He multiplied and spread across the earth, including riding beasts, flocks, trees, fruits, and minerals of many different colors, shapes, qualities, and species, each created and proportioned to serve a distinct human need in this world.

phrases.translation: Surely in this is a sign for those who are mindful
phrases.explanation: In the vast variety of earthly creations, animals, plants, minerals, and provisions that God has placed at humanity’s service is a clear sign and lasting reminder for people who remember God’s favors, take His admonition to heart, and give thanks to Him alone without setting up any partner.

phrases.translation: And He is the One Who has subjected the sea, so from it you may eat tender seafood and extract ornaments to wear.
phrases.explanation: God has subjected the sea and great bodies of salt and fresh water to human beings so that people may catch fresh, tender fish from them for food and dive into their depths to bring out precious ornaments such as pearls and coral to wear as adornment.

phrases.translation: And you see the ships ploughing their way through it, so you may seek His bounty and give thanks ˹to Him˺
phrases.explanation: You also see heavily laden ships cleaving through the waves and parting the water right and left as the winds drive them along, allowing you to travel safely between lands in trade to seek God’s bounty and prompting you to thank Him for His favors.

phrases.translation: He has placed into the earth firm mountains, so it does not shake with you,
phrases.explanation: God cast firm, immovable mountains into the earth like heavy anchors and pegs so that the earth remains stable and does not heave, tilt, or sway beneath the feet of those who live, build, and work upon its surface, as early reports note it swayed before being anchored.

phrases.translation: as well as rivers, and pathways so you may find your way
phrases.explanation: He also caused rivers to flow across the land to water distant valleys and settlements, and opened mountain passes and clear roads across the plains so that travelers can find their way safely from one region to another without getting lost on their journeys by day or night.

phrases.translation: Also by landmarks and stars do people find their way
phrases.explanation: God also established landmarks by which travelers orient themselves. Early commentators explained that these landmarks are mountains and road signs by which people know their way during the daytime, while at night they guide their journeys across land and sea by the positions of the stars.

phrases.translation: Can the One Who creates be equal to those who do not? Will you not then be mindful
phrases.explanation: After recounting these countless creations and blessings, God rebukes the idolaters by asking how the One Who creates all these wonders could ever be treated as equal to lifeless idols that create nothing at all. If they would only reflect, they would realize the folly of worshipping helpless objects beside the Creator.

phrases.translation: If you tried to count Allah’s blessings, you would never be able to number them.
phrases.explanation: If human beings tried to count the blessings God has bestowed upon them in their bodies, senses, health, provisions, and environment, they could never calculate their number or encompass them, let alone fulfill the complete gratitude owed to God for even a small fraction of them.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Despite humanity’s complete inability to thank Him fully as His endless favors deserve, God is All-Forgiving and Most Merciful toward His servants when they repent and turn back to Him in sincere obedience, overlooking their shortcomings in gratitude and sparing them punishment after they return to Him.

phrases.translation: And Allah knows what you conceal and what you reveal
phrases.explanation: God knows every secret thought and intention that people hide within their breasts just as completely as He knows every word and action they display openly. He records whether they meet His blessings with hidden denial or sincere gratitude, and will repay each person accordingly.

phrases.translation: But those ˹idols˺ they invoke besides Allah cannot create anything—they themselves are created
phrases.explanation: As for the idols and false deities that the polytheists call upon besides God, they cannot create even the smallest thing in the heavens or the earth, for they themselves are carved, shaped, and manufactured by human hands. Something that is itself made and powerless can never be a deity.

phrases.translation: They are dead, not alive—not even knowing when their followers will be resurrected
phrases.explanation: Those idols are lifeless objects of stone, wood, or metal without souls, neither hearing nor seeing those who pray to them. They have no awareness of when their worshippers will be raised from their graves for judgment, or according to another reading mentioned by commentators, the disbelievers themselves do not know when they will be resurrected.

phrases.translation: Your God is ˹only˺ One God.
phrases.explanation: After exposing the helplessness of lifeless idols, God proclaims the central truth of all revelation: your true God is One single God alone, without partner, equal, or rival in creation or dominion, and all worship, reverence, and obedience belong exclusively to Him and to none beside Him.

phrases.translation: As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts are in denial, and they are too proud
phrases.explanation: Yet those who do not believe in the hereafter and its reckoning have hearts that stubbornly deny and reject the truth of God’s oneness, and in their haughty arrogance they refuse to humble themselves before their Creator or abandon the false idols of their forefathers.

phrases.translation: Without a doubt, Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal.
phrases.explanation: Without a doubt, it is an established certainty that God knows whatever rejection, malice, and hostility the polytheists conceal inside their hearts against His message, just as completely as He knows the slanders, mockery, and idolatry they proclaim openly with their tongues and outward actions.

phrases.translation: He certainly does not like those who are too proud
phrases.explanation: God certainly does not love those who are arrogant and too proud to submit to His oneness, obey His Messenger, and give up false gods. Rather, He despises their haughty pride and will requite them with disgrace and painful humiliation on the Day of Judgment.

phrases.translation: And when it is said to them, “What has your Lord revealed?” They say, “Ancient fables!”
phrases.explanation: Whenever these arrogant disbelievers were asked by travelers or fellow townspeople what their Lord had sent down to Muhammad, they dismissed the Quran as nothing more than ancient fables, legends, and tales written down by earlier peoples, hoping to turn listeners away from hearing the truth.

phrases.translation: Let them bear their burdens in full on the Day of Judgment as well as some of the burdens of those they mislead without knowledge.
phrases.explanation: By slandering the revelation and barring people from faith, they will end up carrying the full burden of their own sins on Judgment Day along with a share of the sins of the ignorant followers whom they misled, without that reducing the followers’ own punishment in the least.

phrases.translation: Evil indeed is what they will bear
phrases.explanation: Evil indeed is the crushing load of guilt and sin that those misleaders pile upon their own backs for the Day of Resurrection by combining the heavy burden of their own stubborn disbelief with the crime of turning ignorant people away from God’s path without knowledge.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those before them had plotted, but Allah struck at the ˹very˺ foundation of their structure, so the roof collapsed on top of them, and the torment came upon them from where they did not expect
phrases.explanation: Scheming against God’s truth is nothing new, for tyrants before them plotted in the same way. Commentators cited the account of Nimrod, who built a towering structure in defiance of God, until God struck at its foundation and brought the roof crashing down upon them, overtaking them with punishment from a direction they never expected.

phrases.translation: Then on the Day of Judgment He will humiliate them and say, “Where are My ˹so-called˺ associate-gods for whose sake you used to oppose ˹the believers˺?”
phrases.explanation: Beyond worldly ruin, on the Day of Judgment God will publicly disgrace those plotters and ask them in rebuke where the alleged partner-gods are for whose sake they used to oppose God’s prophets and wage hostility against the believers, challenging those idols to save them now.

phrases.translation: Those gifted with knowledge will say, “Surely disgrace and misery today are upon the disbelievers.”
phrases.explanation: At that moment the people endowed with true knowledge of God’s scripture and religion, namely the prophets, angels, scholars, and believers, will declare before all creation that humiliation, shame, abasement, and painful torment on this Day of Judgment fall squarely upon the disbelievers who denied God’s oneness.

phrases.translation: Those whose souls the angels seize while they wrong themselves will then offer ˹full˺ submission ˹and say falsely,˺ “We did not do any evil.”
phrases.explanation: When the angels of death come to seize the souls of those who wronged themselves through idolatry, or as some commentators noted, those in Mecca who marched out with the polytheists at Badr, they suddenly offer submission out of terror and falsely claim that they committed no evil or polytheism.

phrases.translation: ˹The angels will say,˺ “No! Surely Allah fully knows what you used to do
phrases.explanation: The angels immediately refute their desperate lie at the moment of death, declaring that they did indeed commit evil, worship idols, and bar others from God’s path, and reminding them that God has full, exact knowledge of every deed they used to perform in the world.

phrases.translation: So enter the gates of Hell, to stay there forever. Indeed, what an evil home for the arrogant!”
phrases.explanation: The angels command them to enter the seven tiered gates of Hell to remain in its torment forever, each group assigned to its level according to their deeds, and proclaim how wretched a dwelling place the Fire is for those who were too arrogant to worship God alone.

phrases.translation: And ˹when˺ it is said to those mindful ˹of Allah˺, “What has your Lord revealed?” They say, “All the best!”
phrases.explanation: In sharp contrast to the disbelievers, when those who fear God are asked what their Lord has sent down, they testify with gratitude that He has revealed the very best of guidance, mercy, and truth. Early reports note that believers gave this answer to delegations arriving in Mecca, drawing hearts toward Islam.

phrases.translation: For those who do good in this world, there is goodness.
phrases.explanation: For those who do good in this world by believing in God, obeying His commands, and calling others to the truth of Islam, God grants a goodly reward even in this worldly life through honor, peace of heart, victory over their enemies, and wholesome, lawful provision.

phrases.translation: But far better is the ˹eternal˺ Home of the Hereafter. How excellent indeed is the home of the righteous
phrases.explanation: Yet the eternal abode of the hereafter is far greater, nobler, and more lasting than any blessing hastened in this world, and how excellent indeed is Paradise as the final home and reward of the God-fearing who fulfilled their duties and avoided idolatry and sin.

phrases.translation: the Gardens of Eternity which they will enter, under which rivers flow.
phrases.explanation: That excellent home promised to the righteous consists of the Gardens of perpetual residence, which they will enter to dwell in forever while rivers of pure water, milk, wine, and honey flow beneath their shade trees and lofty palaces in eternal peace, honor, and security.

phrases.translation: In it they will have whatever they desire. This is how Allah rewards the righteous—
phrases.explanation: In those eternal gardens of Paradise they will be given whatever their hearts desire and whatever delights their eyes without limit, toil, fatigue, or interruption, for this is how generously God rewards those who feared Him in the world, avoided sin, and fulfilled His commands.

phrases.translation: those whose souls the angels take while they are virtuous, saying ˹to them˺, “Peace be upon you! Enter Paradise for what you used to do.”
phrases.explanation: They are the ones whose souls the angels receive at death while they are pure in faith and free from the filth of polytheism. Both at the moment of death and upon entering the hereafter, the angels greet them with peace and glad tidings, welcoming them into Paradise as the reward for the good deeds they performed.

phrases.translation: Are they only awaiting the coming of the angels or the command of your Lord ˹O Prophet˺?
phrases.explanation: What are these stubborn polytheists of Quraysh waiting for after rejecting every clear proof, except for the angels of death to arrive and seize their souls, or for the command of your Lord to bring worldly punishment or the Day of Resurrection upon them all at once?

phrases.translation: So were those before them. And Allah never wronged them, but it was they who wronged themselves
phrases.explanation: The disbelieving nations before them behaved in the exact same way until ruin overtook them. God did not wrong them in the least by sending down His punishment upon them, rather they wronged their own souls by choosing idolatry and stubborn rebellion against their Creator.

phrases.translation: Then the evil ˹consequences˺ of their deeds overtook them, and they were overwhelmed by what they used to ridicule
phrases.explanation: In the end, the evil punishments they had earned by their own sins struck those earlier nations, and the very torment of God that they used to mock and treat as an empty joke when their messengers warned them surrounded them from every side without escape.

phrases.translation: The polytheists argue, “Had Allah willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have worshipped anything other than Him, nor prohibited anything without His command.”
phrases.explanation: The polytheists tried to excuse their idolatry and their superstitious taboo laws over livestock by arguing that if God had disapproved of their worship of idols or their banning of certain animals without revelation, He would have prevented them and their forefathers from doing so.

phrases.translation: So did those before them. Is not the messengers’ duty only to deliver ˹the message˺ clearly
phrases.explanation: God exposes the emptiness of this excuse by reminding them that earlier deniers made the very same claim while disobeying God’s commands. Since God has sent messengers to make His true will known, the messengers’ only duty is to deliver the message clearly so no one has an excuse.

phrases.translation: We surely sent a messenger to every community, saying, “Worship Allah and shun false gods.”
phrases.explanation: Across history God sent a messenger to every nation with the same foundational command: worship God alone without partner, dedicate obedience purely to Him, and stay far away from Satan, idols, and every false object of worship that lures people into error and eternal ruin.

phrases.translation: But some of them were guided by Allah, while others were destined to stray.
phrases.explanation: After the messengers delivered that clear call to monotheism, humanity divided into two camps: some were guided by God’s grace to believe the messengers, obey Him, and attain salvation, while others chose stubborn denial and followed Satan so that misguidance was justly confirmed upon them.

phrases.translation: So travel throughout the land and see the fate of the deniers
phrases.explanation: God invites the doubters of Quraysh to travel through the lands where ancient nations once lived and see with their own eyes the ruined dwellings and terrible final outcome of those who called God’s messengers liars and persisted in disbelief until divine punishment struck them.

phrases.translation: Even though you ˹O Prophet˺ are keen on their guidance, Allah certainly does not guide those He leaves to stray, and they will have no helpers
phrases.explanation: Even though you, O Prophet, eagerly long for your people to be guided and spared from ruin, whoever God leaves to stray because of their persistent rejection will never find guidance, or under the other canonical reading, has no one who can guide him, and on Judgment Day they will have no helpers to save them from God’s punishment.

phrases.translation: They swear by Allah their most solemn oaths that Allah will never raise the dead to life.
phrases.explanation: The polytheists of Quraysh swore their most solemn, emphatic oaths by God that He would never resurrect anyone after death and decay, using God’s own revered name in vain to deny His almighty power to bring the dead back to life for judgment and recompense.

phrases.translation: Yes ˹He will˺! It is a true promise binding on Him, but most people do not know
phrases.explanation: God refutes their false oath and affirms that He will most certainly raise the dead in fulfillment of a true, binding promise He has decreed upon Himself, even though most people in their ignorance do not know the reality of the resurrection and final judgment.

phrases.translation: ˹He will do that˺ to make clear to them what they disagreed on, and for the disbelievers to know that they were liars
phrases.explanation: God will resurrect all humanity so that He may make unmistakably clear to them the truth of the matters over which believers and disbelievers differed in this world, and so that those who denied the resurrection will know through direct experience that they were liars in their oaths.

phrases.translation: If We ever will something ˹to exist˺, all We say is: “Be!” And it is
phrases.explanation: Resurrecting the dead or creating anything else in the universe requires no effort, fatigue, preparation, or delay from God. Whenever He wills a thing to come into existence, He simply commands it to be, and it immediately comes into being just as He willed without difficulty.

phrases.translation: As for those who emigrated in ˹the cause of˺ Allah after being persecuted, We will surely bless them with a good home in this world.
phrases.explanation: As for the believers who left their homes, families, and homeland for the sake of God after being persecuted and oppressed by the Meccan polytheists, God promises to settle them in a good, honorable home in this world, which early commentators identified as Medina and the victories God granted them.

phrases.translation: But the reward of the Hereafter is far better, if only they knew
phrases.explanation: Yet the eternal reward and high station awaiting those emigrants in the hereafter are vastly greater and more enduring than any worldly home or triumph, if only those who stayed behind in Mecca or persecuted the believers truly understood what God has prepared for the faithful.

phrases.translation: ˹It is˺ they who have patiently endured, and in their Lord they put their trust
phrases.explanation: Those honored emigrants receive this double reward in both worlds because they are the ones who patiently endured persecution, exile, poverty, and hardship for the sake of obeying God, and who place their complete reliance and trust in their Lord alone in every trial they face.

phrases.translation: We did not send ˹messengers˺ before you ˹O Prophet˺ except mere men inspired by Us. If you ˹polytheists˺ do not know ˹this already˺, then ask those who have knowledge ˹of the Scriptures˺
phrases.explanation: When the Meccan polytheists objected that a messenger should be an angel rather than a human being, God reminded the Prophet that every messenger sent before him was likewise a mortal man inspired with divine revelation. If the polytheists do not know this historical fact, they should ask the people of earlier Scripture who know that all prophets were human men.

phrases.translation: ˹We sent them˺ with clear proofs and divine Books.
phrases.explanation: Those human messengers sent before you did not come empty-handed or speak on their own authority, but were sent by God with clear proofs, miracles, and revealed Scriptures establishing the truth of their call to the worship of God alone without any partner or equal.

phrases.translation: And We have sent down to you ˹O Prophet˺ the Reminder, so that you may explain to people what has been revealed for them, and perhaps they will reflect
phrases.explanation: And God has sent down to you, O Prophet, the Reminder, which is the Quran, so that you may explain clearly to people the laws, promises, and warnings revealed for them, and so that they may reflect upon its guidance and take heed before it is too late.

phrases.translation: Do those who devise evil plots feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them? Or that the torment will not come upon them in ways they cannot comprehend
phrases.explanation: Do those who plot evil schemes to persecute the believers and turn people away from Islam feel confident that God will not cause the earth to swallow them up as happened to Korah, or that His punishment will not strike them suddenly from a direction they never anticipated?

phrases.translation: Or that He will not seize them while they go about ˹their day˺, for then they will have no escape
phrases.explanation: Or do those schemers feel secure that God will not seize them with sudden destruction while they are traveling back and forth on their trade caravans by day and night? Whenever God wills to overtake them, they have no power to outrun or frustrate His decree.

phrases.translation: Or that He will not destroy them gradually? But your Lord is truly Ever Gracious, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Or do they feel safe that God will not destroy them gradually by diminishing their numbers, wealth, and surrounding towns little by little, or seizing them while they live in dread after seeing disaster strike their neighbors? Yet your Lord delays their punishment because He is Ever Gracious and Most Merciful.

phrases.translation: Have they not considered how the shadows of everything Allah has created incline to the right and the left ˹as the sun moves˺, totally submitting to Allah in all humility
phrases.explanation: Have those disbelievers not looked at the things God has created, such as mountains, trees, and buildings, and observed how their shadows shift and incline from the right at the start of the day to the left at the end of the day, bowing in humble submission to God’s creative order?

phrases.translation: And to Allah ˹alone˺ bows down ˹in submission˺ whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of living creatures, as do the angels—who are not too proud ˹to do so˺
phrases.explanation: To God alone bows down in submission every living creature that moves in the heavens and on the earth, willingly or by nature, as do all the noble angels in the heavens, who never grow arrogant or consider themselves too proud to worship and obey their Lord.

phrases.translation: They fear their Lord above them, and do whatever they are commanded
phrases.explanation: Those angels in the heavens and obedient creatures revere and fear their Lord Who is high above them in majesty, power, and dominion, dreading His wrath if they were ever to disobey, and they faithfully carry out every command He entrusts to them without fail.

phrases.translation: And Allah has said, “Do not take two gods. There is only One God. So be in awe of Me ˹alone˺.”
phrases.explanation: God has decreed to His servants that they must never take two gods or associate any partner with Him, for He is only One God alone. Therefore people must stand in awe of Him alone and fear His punishment if they worship anything beside Him.

phrases.translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him ˹alone˺ is the everlasting devotion.
phrases.explanation: To God alone belongs everything in the heavens and the earth as His creation, property, and dominion, without any partner or rival, and to Him alone belongs perpetual, sincere obedience and pure devotion at all times from all creatures in the heavens and the earth.

phrases.translation: Will you then fear any other than Allah
phrases.explanation: Since God alone owns all creation, provides all sustenance, holds life and death in His hand, and deserves constant obedience, how can you fear, revere, or worship powerless beings other than God that control neither harm nor benefit for anyone in the heavens or the earth?

phrases.translation: Whatever blessings you have are from Allah.
phrases.explanation: Every single blessing that human beings enjoy in their bodies, senses, health, children, wealth, safety, and daily livelihood comes solely from God’s grace and generosity, not from any lifeless idol or false god that they set up beside Him in their ignorance and ingratitude, for those idols can neither benefit nor harm anyone.

phrases.translation: Then whenever hardship touches you, to Him ˹alone˺ you cry ˹for help˺
phrases.explanation: Yet when sickness, famine, danger at sea, or severe hardship strikes you, you immediately forget your lifeless idols and cry out fervently and aloud to God alone to rescue you, knowing deep in your hearts that none but He can remove distress and save you.

phrases.translation: Then as soon as He removes the hardship from you, a group of you associates ˹others˺ with their Lord ˹in worship˺
phrases.explanation: Then as soon as God answers your desperate cries and lifts the affliction, sickness, or danger from you, a group of you goes right back to associating idols and partners with their Lord in worship, ungratefully forgetting the mercy and deliverance He just showed them.

phrases.translation: only returning Our favours with ingratitude.
phrases.explanation: By returning to idol worship right after God rescues them from distress and answers their desperate prayers, they show utter ingratitude for the blessings and deliverance We granted them, denying God’s favor and attributing their relief to false gods, intercessors, or mere chance instead of thanking their Lord.

phrases.translation: So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know
phrases.explanation: God issues a stern threat telling them to enjoy their brief worldly pleasures, wealth, and delusions for a little while longer, for they will soon know the bitter consequence of their ingratitude when they face the painful punishment of the Fire in the hereafter on Judgment Day.

phrases.translation: And they ˹even˺ assign to those ˹idols˺—who know nothing—a share of what We have provided for them.
phrases.explanation: In their ignorance, the polytheists even set aside a portion of the crops and livestock that God Himself created and provided for them and dedicate that share as offerings to lifeless idols that know nothing and have no power at all to help or harm.

phrases.translation: By Allah! You will certainly be questioned about whatever ˹lies˺ you used to fabricate ˹against Allah˺
phrases.explanation: God swears solemnly by Himself that on the Day of Judgment they will certainly be called to account and questioned about these false practices, invented offerings to lifeless idols, and lies they fabricated against Him without any revealed authority or proof from God to justify their claims.

phrases.translation: And they attribute ˹angels as˺ daughters to Allah—glory be to Him!—the opposite of what they desire for themselves
phrases.explanation: The Arab polytheists even claimed in their ignorance that the noble angels were the daughters of God, glory be to Him far above their slander, while reserving for themselves what they preferred and desired, namely sons, and attributing to God what they themselves despised and hated.

phrases.translation: Whenever one of them is given the good news of a baby girl, his face grows gloomy, as he suppresses his rage
phrases.explanation: Their hypocrisy is exposed by how they react when one of them is told that his wife has given birth to a baby girl: his face turns dark with gloom, shame, and disappointment while he silently chokes back rage and grief inside himself over the news.

phrases.translation: He hides himself from the people because of the bad news he has received.
phrases.explanation: He hides himself away from his tribesmen and avoids their company out of shame, grief, and embarrassment over the news of a newborn daughter, dreading their mockery and considering her birth a terrible disgrace and misfortune to his household according to the corrupt customs of pre-Islamic ignorance.

phrases.translation: Should he keep her in disgrace, or bury her ˹alive˺ in the ground?
phrases.explanation: He debates within himself whether to let his newborn daughter live in disgrace and humiliation, deprived of inheritance, honor, and respect among her people, or to bury her alive in the dust of the ground as was practiced by cruel men in the era of pre-Islamic ignorance.

phrases.translation: Evil indeed is their judgment
phrases.explanation: How evil, corrupt, and unjust is their judgment when they reserve sons for themselves while attributing to the Almighty Creator of the universe the very daughters they hate so fiercely that they bury them alive in the ground out of shame, fear of poverty, and arrogance!

phrases.translation: To those who disbelieve in the Hereafter belong all evil qualities, whereas to Allah belong the finest attributes.
phrases.explanation: To those who disbelieve in the hereafter and deny the Resurrection belong the worst qualities of ignorance, cruelty, neediness, and contradiction, whereas to God belong the highest, most exalted attributes of absolute perfection, oneness, majesty, and self-sufficiency far above every defect, need, child, or partner in creation.

phrases.translation: And He is the Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: And He is the Almighty in His sovereign dominion and irresistible retribution against those who defy Him and worship idols, and the All-Wise in all that He creates, governs, commands, and decrees for His servants across the heavens and the earth without any flaw or error.

phrases.translation: If Allah were to punish people ˹immediately˺ for their wrongdoing, He would not have left a single living being on earth.
phrases.explanation: If God were to punish human beings immediately in this world for their idolatry, tyranny, and sins without granting them respite, His wrath would sweep away every living creature on the face of the earth, including the beasts of the land along with sinful humanity.

phrases.translation: But He delays them for an appointed term. And when their time arrives, they cannot delay it for a moment, nor could they advance it
phrases.explanation: Instead, in His forbearance and mercy He delays their reckoning until a fixed, appointed term that He has decreed for them in His knowledge, and when that deadline finally arrives, they cannot push it back by a single moment nor bring it forward before its appointed time.

phrases.translation: They attribute to Allah what they hate ˹for themselves˺, and their tongues utter the lie that they will have the finest reward.
phrases.explanation: They attribute to God the daughters they hate for themselves, while their tongues utter the brazen lie that the best share, whether sons in this world or a goodly reward in the hereafter if there is one, belongs to them instead of the believers while falsely claiming that God approves of their custom and will grant them goodness if they return to Him.

phrases.translation: Without a doubt, for them is the Fire, where they will be abandoned
phrases.explanation: Without a doubt, what truly awaits them in the hereafter is the Fire of Hell, where they will be hastened into punishment ahead of others, or left abandoned, neglected, and forgotten in torment forever because of the lies they uttered against God where no intercessor or idol can ever rescue them from the flames.

phrases.translation: By Allah! We have surely sent messengers to communities before you ˹O Prophet˺, but Satan made their misdeeds appealing to them.
phrases.explanation: God swears solemnly by Himself to console the Prophet that messengers were sent to many nations before him with the call to monotheism, but Satan beautified their idol worship and evil deeds in their eyes until they rejected the truth and belied the messengers just as the polytheists of Mecca now reject the Quran.

phrases.translation: So he is their patron today, and they will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: So Satan is the patron, leader, and companion of these disbelievers today in this world, a wretched patron who cannot help or defend them at all when they suffer a painful, unending punishment in the hereafter for following his whispers into ruin when they stand before their Lord on the Day of Judgment.

phrases.translation: We have revealed to you the Book only to clarify for them what they differed about, and as a guide and mercy for those who believe
phrases.explanation: God has sent down the Quran to you, O Prophet, only so that you may make clear to humanity the truth regarding resurrection, God’s oneness, and the religious laws over which they differed, and so that the Scripture serves as unfailing guidance and mercy for people who believe.

phrases.translation: And Allah sends down rain from the sky, giving life to the earth after its death. Surely in this is a sign for those who listen
phrases.explanation: Pointing again to His signs in creation, God reminds humanity that He sends down rain from the sky and revives the barren, lifeless earth with blooming vegetation after its death. Just as He brings dead soil back to life, He will raise the dead, a clear sign for people who listen with understanding and receptivity.

phrases.translation: And there is certainly a lesson for you in cattle: We give you to drink of what is in their bellies, from between digested food and blood: pure milk, pleasant to drink
phrases.explanation: In livestock too there is a profound lesson for you to reflect upon: from within their bellies, out of the nutrients separated cleanly between the digested food in the intestines and the blood in the veins, God produces pure, white milk that is free of any trace of blood or filth and pleasant for those who drink it.

phrases.translation: And from the fruits of palm trees and grapevines you derive intoxicants as well as wholesome provision. Surely in this is a sign for those who understand
phrases.explanation: And from the fruits of date palms and grapevines you make intoxicating drink as well as wholesome, lawful nourishment such as fresh fruit, dried raisins, vinegar, and sweet syrup. Early commentators noted that this verse mentioned intoxicants before wine was later prohibited, reminding people of the sign of God’s power for those who use their reason.

phrases.translation: And your Lord inspired the bees: “Make ˹your˺ homes in the mountains, the trees, and in what people construct
phrases.explanation: Your Lord inspired the bees by casting instinctive guidance into their hearts, directing them to build their hives and honeycombs in the rocky crevices of the mountains, in the hollows of trees, and in the trellises, roofs, and hives that human beings construct for them.

phrases.translation: and feed from ˹the flower of˺ any fruit ˹you please˺ and follow the ways your Lord has made easy for you.”
phrases.explanation: God further inspired the bee to feed from every kind of fruit and blossom and to travel along the pathways across valleys and mountains that her Lord has made easy and submissive for her, so that she never loses her way back to her hive.

phrases.translation: From their bellies comes forth liquid of varying colours, in which there is healing for people. Surely in this is a sign for those who reflect
phrases.explanation: From the bellies of the bees comes forth delicious honey of varying shades of white, yellow, and red according to their pasture and season, containing healing for people’s illnesses. In this marvel is a clear sign of God’s wisdom and power for those who reflect.

phrases.translation: Allah has created you, and then causes you to die.
phrases.explanation: God alone created you from nothing when you did not exist and then takes your souls at the end of your appointed lifespans, proving that both life and death rest entirely in His hand rather than with any powerless idol that cannot create anything and calling humanity to worship the Creator alone.

phrases.translation: And some of you are left to reach the most feeble stage of life so that they may know nothing after having known much. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, Most Capable
phrases.explanation: Among you are some who are left to live into the most feeble, decrepit stage of old age, when memory and strength fade until a person knows nothing after once possessing abundant knowledge, just like a small child. God alone is All-Knowing Whose knowledge never fades, and Most Capable of all things.

phrases.translation: And Allah has favoured some of you over others in provision. But those who have been much favoured would not share their wealth with those ˹bondspeople˺ in their possession, making them their equals.
phrases.explanation: God has favored some people over others in worldly wealth and sustenance. Yet those blessed with abundant riches refuse to hand over an equal share of their wealth to their own slaves so that masters and slaves become equal partners in everything they own or share equal authority over their property and households.

phrases.translation: Do they then deny Allah’s favours
phrases.explanation: How then can the polytheists refuse to make their own servants equal partners in the wealth God gave them, while setting up God’s created servants and lifeless idols as equal partners to Him in worship, denying God’s favors through such blatant ingratitude while knowing full well that God alone granted them every blessing?

phrases.translation: And Allah has made for you spouses of your own kind, and given you through your spouses children and grandchildren.
phrases.explanation: God created for you spouses of your own human kind, beginning with Eve created from Adam, and blessed you through your spouses with sons, daughters, grandchildren, and sons-in-law who serve, assist, and continue your families and lineages across generations in this world as a great favor and mercy from your Lord.

phrases.translation: And He has granted you good, lawful provisions. Are they then faithful to falsehood and ungrateful for Allah’s favours
phrases.explanation: He also provided you with pure, wholesome foods and lawful blessings of every kind, yet after receiving all these favors from God alone, do the polytheists still believe in false idols and ungratefully deny the blessings of God Who created and sustained them instead of thanking Him alone through sincere obedience?

phrases.translation: Yet they worship besides Allah those ˹idols˺ who do not afford them any provision from the heavens and the earth, nor do they have the power to
phrases.explanation: Despite all of God’s blessings, the idolaters worship besides Him lifeless idols that do not control a single drop of rain from the heavens or a single plant from the earth to provide for them, nor do they have the capacity to ever gain such power.

phrases.translation: So do not set up equals to Allah, for Allah certainly knows and you do not know
phrases.explanation: Therefore do not invent likenesses, equals, or partners for God, for He has no peer in creation or divinity. God knows the truth of His absolute oneness and the reality of what you do, whereas you do not know the grave consequences of setting up rivals to Him.

phrases.translation: Allah sets forth a parable: a slave who lacks all means, compared to a ˹free˺ man to whom We granted a good provision, of which he donates ˹freely,˺ openly and secretly.
phrases.explanation: God sets forth a parable contrasting an owned slave who possesses nothing and has no power to spend or act on his own with a free man whom God has blessed with generous, lawful wealth, from which he gives in charity by night and day, in secret and in public.

phrases.translation: Are they equal? Praise be to Allah. In fact, most of them do not know
phrases.explanation: Can those two ever be equal? Some commentators explained this as a comparison between the powerless idol and the Almighty Creator, while others explained it as contrasting the disbeliever who does no good with the grateful believer. All praise belongs to God alone, though most of them do not know.

phrases.translation: And Allah sets forth a parable of two men: one of them is dumb, incapable of anything. He is a burden on his master. Wherever he is sent, he brings no good.
phrases.explanation: God sets forth a second parable of two men: one is mute and incapable of anything, neither understanding nor speaking, a heavy burden upon his guardian, bringing back no good wherever he is sent. Early commentators explained that this represents the lifeless idol made of stone or wood that must be carried by its worshipper.

phrases.translation: Can such a person be equal to the one who commands justice and is on the Straight Path
phrases.explanation: Can such a helpless mute who understands nothing and accomplishes nothing ever be equal to the One Who speaks the truth, commands justice and fairness, and stands upon the straight, upright path, namely God the Almighty, or the true believer who upholds monotheism and calls humanity to worship the One true Creator alone?

phrases.translation: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs ˹the knowledge of˺ the unseen in the heavens and the earth.
phrases.explanation: To God alone belongs complete knowledge and dominion over everything hidden and unseen in the heavens and the earth, including the exact time of the Resurrection, which no idol, angel, or human being knows or shares with Him in any way whatsoever and to Him alone belongs the sovereign command over both worlds.

phrases.translation: Bringing about the Hour would only take the blink of an eye, or even less. Surely Allah is Most Capable of everything
phrases.explanation: Bringing about the Hour of Judgment and raising all creation from their graves takes no longer for God than the blink of an eye, or even less, because He simply commands it to be and it happens at once. Surely God is Most Capable of everything.

phrases.translation: And Allah brought you out of the wombs of your mothers while you knew nothing, and gave you hearing, sight, and intellect so perhaps you would be thankful
phrases.explanation: God brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers as helpless infants knowing nothing at all, and then endowed you with ears to hear, eyes to see, and hearts and minds to understand right from wrong, so that you would recognize His favors and give thanks to Him through obedience.

phrases.translation: Have they not seen the birds glide in the open sky? None holds them up except Allah. Surely in this are signs for those who believe
phrases.explanation: Have people not looked up at the birds gliding effortlessly through the open air between heaven and earth, spreading and folding their wings? None holds them aloft in the sky except God, Who created their bodies and subjected the air to carry them, providing clear signs for people who believe.

phrases.translation: And Allah has made your homes a place to rest, and has given you tents from the hide of animals, light to handle when you travel and when you camp.
phrases.explanation: God has made your permanent houses of stone, brick, and clay places of rest, shelter, and tranquility in your towns, and also gave you portable tents made from the hides of livestock that are light and easy to carry when you travel and when you pitch camp.

phrases.translation: And out of their wool, fur, and hair He has given you furnishings and goods for a while
phrases.explanation: And from the wool of sheep, the fur of camels, and the hair of goats He has provided you with carpets, blankets, warm clothing, household furnishings, and articles of trade to enjoy until your appointed time in this world comes to an end when you leave behind your earthly goods at death.

phrases.translation: And Allah has provided you shade out of what He created, and has given you shelter in the mountains. He has also provided you with clothes protecting you from the heat ˹and cold˺, and armour shielding you in battle.
phrases.explanation: Continuing to recount His blessings, God reminds you that He provided shade from trees, clouds, and walls to shelter you from heat, caves and dwellings in the mountains for refuge, garments of cotton, linen, and wool to protect you from heat and cold, and coats of iron mail to shield you from weapons in battle.

phrases.translation: This is how He perfects His favour upon you, so perhaps you will ˹fully˺ submit ˹to Him˺
phrases.explanation: In this way God completes His outward and inward favors upon you in every necessity of life, shelter, clothing, and safety, so that you may recognize His grace, abandon false idols, and submit wholeheartedly to Him in Islam and sincere obedience and thank Him for protecting your bodies and your lives.

phrases.translation: But if they turn away, then your duty ˹O Prophet˺ is only to deliver ˹the message˺ clearly
phrases.explanation: If the polytheists still turn their backs on faith and obedience after hearing all these clear proofs and reminders of God’s favors, no blame rests upon you, O Prophet, for your sole responsibility is to deliver the message clearly so that everyone understands it and no one has any excuse left before God.

phrases.translation: They are aware of Allah’s favours, but still deny them. And most of them are ˹truly˺ ungrateful
phrases.explanation: They know very well in their hearts that all these blessings of homes, livestock, rain, and protection come from God alone, or according to another view, they recognize the truthfulness of Muhammad’s prophethood, yet they stubbornly deny it by attributing those blessings to their idols and forefathers.

phrases.translation: ˹Consider, O Prophet,˺ the Day We will call ˹a prophet as˺ a witness from every faith-community. Then the disbelievers will neither be allowed to plead nor appease ˹their Lord˺
phrases.explanation: Warn them of the Day of Judgment when God will raise up a prophet from every nation to testify that he delivered God’s message to his people. On that Day the disbelievers will not be permitted to offer excuses, nor will they be allowed to return to make amends and seek God’s pleasure.

phrases.translation: And when the wrongdoers face the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be delayed ˹from it˺
phrases.explanation: When those wrongdoers who committed idolatry and denied the truth face the torment of the Fire with their own eyes on Judgment Day, its severity will never be lightened for them even for a moment, nor will they be granted any delay or reprieve once punishment begins.

phrases.translation: And when the polytheists see their associate-gods, they will say, “Our Lord! These are our associate-gods that we used to invoke besides You.”
phrases.explanation: When the polytheists see the idols and false deities they used to worship brought before the Fire on Judgment Day, they will point to them in desperation and say to their Lord that these were the partner-gods they used to invoke besides Him in the hope that those idols might share their blame.

phrases.translation: Their gods will throw a rebuttal at them, ˹saying,˺ “You are definitely liars.”
phrases.explanation: God will enable those false gods to speak and cast their words right back in their faces, declaring before all creation that their worshippers were utter liars in calling them gods because they never possessed divinity or told anyone to worship them besides God and thus their false hopes will collapse into utter disgrace.

phrases.translation: They will offer ˹full˺ submission to Allah on that Day, and whatever ˹gods˺ they fabricated will fail them
phrases.explanation: On that Day the idolaters will humble themselves and offer complete submission to God when submission can no longer benefit them, and all the false gods, claims, and intercessors they used to fabricate in the world will vanish and abandon them to the Fire without any helper or protector to ward off God’s decree.

phrases.translation: For those who disbelieve and hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah, We will add more punishment to their punishment for all the corruption they spread
phrases.explanation: As for those who disbelieved in God and actively hindered others from following the path of Islam, God will add further punishment on top of their punishment for disbelief, which early commentators described as scorpions and serpents in Hell, in recompense for the corruption they spread by leading others astray.

phrases.translation: ˹Consider, O Prophet,˺ the Day We will call against every faith-community a witness of their own. And We will call you to be a witness against these ˹people of yours˺.
phrases.explanation: Remember the Day of Resurrection when God will raise up from within every community their own prophet as a witness over how they answered him, and will bring you, O Prophet, as a witness over your community and people regarding how they received the Quran.

phrases.translation: We have revealed to you the Book as an explanation of all things, a guide, a mercy, and good news for those who ˹fully˺ submit
phrases.explanation: For God has sent down to you the Quran as a clear explanation of everything people need to know regarding lawful and unlawful matters, guidance, reward, and punishment, serving as a guide, a mercy, and glad tidings for those who submit to God in word and deed and follow His revealed law.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah commands justice, grace, as well as courtesy to close relatives. He forbids indecency, wickedness, and aggression.
phrases.explanation: In this comprehensive verse God commands justice, beginning with testifying to His oneness and treating everyone fairly, along with excellence in obedience, forgiving kindness, and giving to close relatives, while forbidding shameful indecency, every form of sin, and tyrannical transgression against others in every sphere of faith, family life, and society.

phrases.translation: He instructs you so perhaps you will be mindful
phrases.explanation: Through these clear commands of virtue and prohibitions of vice, God counsels, reminds, and instructs you so that you may reflect upon your duty to Him, remember His favors, and hold fast to righteousness in word and deed throughout your lives and earn the lasting pleasure and reward of your Lord.

phrases.translation: Honour Allah’s covenant when you make a pledge, and do not break your oaths after confirming them, having made Allah your guarantor. Surely Allah knows all you do
phrases.explanation: Fulfill the covenant of God whenever you enter into a pledge, allegiance, or treaty, and never break your oaths after you have solemnly confirmed them. By swearing in God’s name you have appointed God as your witness and guarantor, and He knows everything you do.

phrases.translation: Do not be like the woman who ˹foolishly˺ unravels her yarn after it is firmly spun, by taking your oaths as a means of deceiving one another in favour of a stronger group.
phrases.explanation: Do not be like a foolish woman who spins her yarn until it is strong and tightly twisted and then unravels it into tangled shreds, by using your oaths as a trick of deceit among yourselves, breaking a treaty with one group whenever you find another group richer and more numerous.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah tests you through this. And on the Day of Judgment He will certainly make your differences clear to you
phrases.explanation: God tests your faithfulness to your covenants through the greater numbers, strength, and wealth He grants to others, so that the sincere are distinguished from the treacherous, and on the Day of Judgment He will make clear to you the truth of all that you differed over.

phrases.translation: Had Allah willed, He could have easily made you one community ˹of believers˺, but He leaves to stray whoever He wills and guides whoever He wills.
phrases.explanation: Had God willed, He could have made all humanity one single community united upon faith and obedience, but in His wisdom He leaves to stray those who choose rebellion and guides by His grace those who seek the truth and turn to Him so that each person is justly requited for their choice.

phrases.translation: And you will certainly be questioned about what you used to do
phrases.explanation: And on the Day of Resurrection you will certainly be questioned by your Lord about all the deeds you used to do in this world, so that the obedient are rewarded and the disobedient are held to account according to their actions without anyone being wronged or overlooked in the least.

phrases.translation: And do not take your oaths as a means of deceiving one another or your feet will slip after they have been firm.
phrases.explanation: God repeats the warning never to use oaths and pledges as a means of mutual deception and betrayal among people, lest your feet slip into ruin and trial after having stood firm upon the path of Islam, guidance, and safety and thus bring destruction upon yourselves in both worlds.

phrases.translation: Then you will taste the evil ˹consequences˺ of hindering ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah, and you will suffer a tremendous punishment
phrases.explanation: If you betray your pledges, you will taste painful punishment in this world for turning people away from God’s religion when they see treachery among believers, and a tremendous torment will await you with God in the hereafter on Judgment Day as a just recompense for breaking your solemn covenants.

phrases.translation: And do not trade Allah’s covenant for a fleeting gain. What is with Allah is certainly far better for you, if only you knew
phrases.explanation: Never sell or break the covenant of God in exchange for a paltry, fleeting worldly benefit, for all the wealth of this world is small. The eternal reward with God for honoring your pledges is far better for you, if you truly know what is lasting.

phrases.translation: Whatever you have will end, but whatever Allah has is everlasting.
phrases.explanation: Whatever worldly wealth, power, and pleasure you possess will inevitably run out, vanish, and perish, whereas the reward, honor, and treasure stored with God in Paradise for those who keep their covenants are everlasting and never diminish or pass away for anyone who prefers the hereafter over fleeting gain.

phrases.translation: And We will certainly reward the steadfast according to the best of their deeds
phrases.explanation: And God will surely reward those who patiently kept their covenants, avoided forbidden gain, and endured hardship in obedience to Him on the Day of Resurrection according to the very best of the righteous deeds they performed in the world and multiply their recompense out of His boundless grace.

phrases.translation: Whoever does good, whether male or female, and is a believer, We will surely bless them with a good life, and We will certainly reward them according to the best of their deeds
phrases.explanation: Whoever performs righteous deeds in obedience to God, whether male or female, while holding sincere faith in heart, God promises to bless them with a good, wholesome life, which early interpreters explained as contentment and lawful provision in this world or joy in Paradise, and to reward them in the hereafter according to their finest deeds.

phrases.translation: When you recite the Quran, seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the accursed
phrases.explanation: Whenever you are about to recite the Quran, seek refuge with God from the whispers and interference of Satan, the outcast driven far from God’s mercy. Early scholars noted this directive teaches believers to turn to God’s protection so their hearts remain attentive to His words.

phrases.translation: He certainly has no authority over those who believe and put their trust in their Lord
phrases.explanation: Satan possesses no compelling power, proof, or dominance over those who truly believe in God and place their reliance and trust in their Lord alone, for their sincere faith and seeking refuge in God shield them from his plots and keep them from unforgiven sin.

phrases.translation: His authority is only over those who take him as a patron and who—under his influence—associate ˹others˺ with Allah ˹in worship˺
phrases.explanation: Satan’s influence, proof, and authority extend only over those who willingly take him as their patron and leader, obeying his whispers instead of God’s commands, and who because of their obedience to him associate false partners with God in worship and thus bring ruin upon themselves by their own choice.

phrases.translation: When We replace a verse with another—and Allah knows best what He reveals—
phrases.explanation: Whenever God lifts the ruling or wording of one revealed verse and puts another in its place according to what best serves His servants at each stage, and God knows best the wisdom of what He sends down and abrogates for humanity according to what brings the greatest benefit and mercy,

phrases.translation: they say, “You ˹Muḥammad˺ are just a fabricator.” In fact, most of them do not know
phrases.explanation: The ignorant polytheists claim that Muhammad is merely fabricating the Quran on his own because he commands something one day and replaces it with an easier or firmer ruling later. In reality, most of them do not know God’s wisdom in revelation and therefore slander the Messenger out of sheer ignorance.

phrases.translation: Say, “The holy spirit has brought it down from your Lord with the truth to reassure the believers, and as a guide and good news for those who submit ˹to Allah˺.”
phrases.explanation: Tell them, O Prophet, that the Holy Spirit, the angel Gabriel, has brought the Quran down from your Lord in complete truth, including both its abrogating and abrogated verses, to make the believers firm in faith and to serve as guidance and glad tidings for those who submit to God.

phrases.translation: And We surely know that they say, “No one is teaching him except a human.”
phrases.explanation: God knows well that the Meccan polytheists falsely claim that a mortal man, whom early reports identify as a foreign Christian blacksmith or servant living in Mecca whom the Prophet used to visit, is the one teaching Muhammad the Quran and passing off human tales as divine revelation.

phrases.translation: But the man they refer to speaks a foreign tongue, whereas this ˹Quran˺ is ˹in˺ eloquent Arabic
phrases.explanation: God exposes the absurdity of their slander with a simple, undeniable fact: the man they point to speaks a foreign tongue and can barely express himself in Arabic, whereas this Quran is revealed in clear, unmatched, eloquent Arabic that no human can imitate in its wisdom, eloquence, and truthfulness.

phrases.translation: Surely those who do not believe in Allah’s revelations will never be guided by Allah, and they will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: Surely those who stubbornly refuse to believe in God’s verses, revelations, and clear proofs will not be guided by God to the path of truth while they persist in denial, and in the hereafter they will suffer a painful, agonizing punishment when they stand before their Lord on Judgment Day.

phrases.translation: No one fabricates lies except those who disbelieve in Allah’s revelations, and it is they who are the ˹true˺ liars
phrases.explanation: Turning the polytheists’ accusation back upon them, God declares that His Prophet never invents falsehood, for only those who disbelieve in God’s signs and neither hope for His reward nor fear His punishment fabricate lies against God, and they are the true liars in the sight of God and all people of understanding.

phrases.translation: Whoever disbelieves in Allah after their belief—not those who are forced while their hearts are firm in faith,
phrases.explanation: Whoever renounces faith in God after having believed incurs terrible wrath, except for one who is subjected to torture and forced to utter words of disbelief with the tongue while his heart remains firm and tranquil in faith, as happened to Ammar ibn Yasir under Meccan persecution.

phrases.translation: but those who embrace disbelief wholeheartedly—they will be condemned by Allah and suffer a tremendous punishment
phrases.explanation: Rather, those who open their breasts willingly to disbelief, find comfort in renouncing Islam, and embrace apostasy in their hearts bring the terrible wrath of God upon themselves and will suffer a tremendous punishment in the hereafter for their betrayal after having known and professed the truth of faith.

phrases.translation: This is because they prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter. Surely Allah never guides those who ˹choose to˺ disbelieve
phrases.explanation: That wrath and tremendous punishment fall upon them because they deliberately preferred the comfort, wealth, and approval of this worldly life over the eternal reward of the hereafter, and because God does not guide a people who choose disbelief over faith after the clear proofs of God have reached them.

phrases.translation: They are the ones whose hearts, ears, and eyes are sealed by Allah, and it is they who are ˹truly˺ heedless
phrases.explanation: Because of their willful choice of worldly life over faith, they are the ones whose hearts, hearing, and sight God has sealed shut, so they neither understand nor benefit from reminders, and they remain completely heedless of the punishment prepared for them when they are raised up to face their Lord.

phrases.translation: Without a doubt, they will be the losers in the Hereafter
phrases.explanation: Without a doubt, it is an inescapable certainty that in the hereafter these apostates and stubborn disbelievers will be the ultimate losers who have destroyed their own souls and forfeited their share of eternal honor and mercy with God on Judgment Day and no regret on that Day will avail them.

phrases.translation: As for those who emigrated after being compelled ˹to renounce Islam˺, then struggled ˹in Allah’s cause˺, and persevered, your Lord ˹O Prophet˺ is truly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful after all
phrases.explanation: As for the vulnerable believers in Mecca who were tortured into uttering what the idolaters demanded, and then escaped by emigrating to Medina, strove in God’s cause, and patiently endured hardship, your Lord after that trial and repentance is truly All-Forgiving and Most Merciful toward them.

phrases.translation: ˹Consider˺ the Day ˹when˺ every soul will come pleading for itself, and each will be paid in full for what it did, and none will be wronged
phrases.explanation: Remember the Day of Resurrection when every soul will come forward pleading only for itself, concerned with its own salvation rather than family or allies, and every soul will be repaid in full for all the good or evil it did without being wronged in the least.

phrases.translation: And Allah sets forth the example of a society which was safe and at ease, receiving its provision in abundance from all directions.
phrases.explanation: God sets forth the parable of a town, which early commentators identified as Mecca, that lived in complete security from raids while surrounding tribes fought one another, enjoying peaceful stability as abundant fruits, goods, and provisions flowed into it from every direction without its people needing to raid or fear attack.

phrases.translation: But its people met Allah’s favours with ingratitude, so Allah made them taste the clutches of hunger and fear for their misdeeds
phrases.explanation: Yet its inhabitants met God’s blessings with ungrateful denial by rejecting His Messenger and persecuting the believers, so God made them taste all-encompassing hunger during a severe seven-year famine and constant fear of the Muslim armies because of their evil deeds until their nobles were struck down by the sword at Badr.

phrases.translation: A messenger of their own actually did come to them, but they denied him. So the torment overtook them while they persisted in wrongdoing
phrases.explanation: Indeed, a noble messenger from their own tribe, whose honesty and lineage they knew well, came to them calling them to God, but they called him a liar, so the punishment of famine, fear, and defeat at Badr seized them while they persisted in idolatry.

phrases.translation: So eat from the good, lawful things which Allah has provided for you, and be grateful for Allah’s favours, if you ˹truly˺ worship Him ˹alone˺
phrases.explanation: Therefore eat, O believers, from the lawful, wholesome provisions and ritually slaughtered livestock that God has granted you, free of the false taboos invented by the pagans, and thank God for His favors in word and deed if it is truly Him alone that you worship.

phrases.translation: He has only forbidden you ˹to eat˺ carrion, blood, swine, and what is slaughtered in the name of any other than Allah.
phrases.explanation: God refutes the polytheists’ invented food taboos by declaring that He has only forbidden you to eat dead animals that died without proper slaughter, poured-out blood, pork, and animals slaughtered for idols or in the name of anyone other than God as part of the pagan customs of pre-Islamic ignorance.

phrases.translation: But if someone is compelled by necessity—neither driven by desire nor exceeding immediate need—then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Even so, if famine or starvation forces someone to eat from these forbidden things out of dire necessity to save life, without desiring sin or eating more than needed to survive, God is All-Forgiving and Most Merciful toward His servant and does not punish him for preserving his life.

phrases.translation: Do not falsely declare with your tongues, “This is lawful, and that is unlawful,” ˹only˺ fabricating lies against Allah. Indeed, those who fabricate lies against Allah will never succeed
phrases.explanation: Do not let your tongues utter the falsehoods you invent regarding livestock and crops by declaring on your own authority that this animal is lawful and that one is unlawful, thereby fabricating lies against God. Those who invent lies against God will never prosper either in this worldly life or in the hereafter.

phrases.translation: ˹It is only˺ a brief enjoyment, then they will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: All that such fabricators gain from their false religious laws and worldly indulgence is a brief, paltry enjoyment that quickly vanishes at death, and then when they return to God in the hereafter they will suffer a painful, unending punishment for the lies and superstitions they attributed to Him.

phrases.translation: To the Jews, We have forbidden what We related to you before. We did not wrong them, but it was they who wronged themselves
phrases.explanation: As for the Jews, God had forbidden them certain foods that He already recounted to you in Surah al-Anam, namely every animal with claws and the fat of cattle and sheep. God did not wrong them by imposing those restrictions, rather they wronged themselves through their own transgression and disobedience.

phrases.translation: As for those who commit evil ignorantly ˹or recklessly˺, then repent afterwards and mend their ways, then your Lord is surely All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Yet toward those who commit evil and disobedience out of ignorance and foolishness, for everyone who disobeys God acts in folly, and then repent afterward and mend their conduct through sincere obedience, your Lord after their repentance is surely All-Forgiving and Most Merciful and wipes away the sins they committed before repenting.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Abraham was a model of excellence: devoted to Allah, ˹perfectly˺ upright—not a polytheist—
phrases.explanation: Refuting Quraysh’s false claim to follow Abraham, God declares that Abraham was in himself a complete model of virtue and a teacher of good, devoutly obedient to God and uprightly devoted to pure Islam, and he was never one of the polytheists whom the idolaters of Mecca falsely claimed to follow.

phrases.translation: ˹utterly˺ grateful for Allah’s favours. ˹So˺ He chose him and guided him to the Straight Path
phrases.explanation: Abraham was constantly grateful for all of God’s favors, attributing every blessing to God alone without setting up any idol or partner. Therefore God chose him as His close friend and prophet and guided him to the straight path of pure monotheism and made him an enduring example for all believers.

phrases.translation: We blessed him with all goodness in this world, and in the Hereafter he will certainly be among the righteous
phrases.explanation: God granted Abraham goodness in this world, which early commentators explained as a truthful reputation of honor and high esteem among all religious communities, and in the hereafter he is certainly among the righteous in the highest ranks of Paradise alongside the prophets and close friends of God.

phrases.translation: Then We revealed to you ˹O Prophet, saying˺: “Follow the faith of Abraham, the upright, who was not one of the polytheists.”
phrases.explanation: Then We revealed to you, O Prophet, commanding you and your community to follow the upright religion of Abraham in pure monotheism, worshipping God alone and disowning every false idol, for Abraham was never one of the polytheists in belief or practice and therefore Quraysh have no share in his way.

phrases.translation: ˹Honouring˺ the Sabbath was ordained only for those who disputed about Abraham. And surely your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Judgment regarding their disputes
phrases.explanation: Observing the Saturday Sabbath was imposed only upon the Jews after they differed with their prophet over Friday, which had been prescribed for them, and chose Saturday instead. On the Day of Resurrection your Lord will surely judge between them regarding all that they disputed over.

phrases.translation: Invite ˹all˺ to the Way of your Lord with wisdom and kind advice, and only debate with them in the best manner.
phrases.explanation: God commands the Prophet and his followers to call people to the way of Islam with wisdom, meaning the clear proofs of the Book and prophetic teaching, and with kind, moving admonition, and to debate with opponents in the most gracious, patient manner, overlooking personal insults.

phrases.translation: Surely your Lord ˹alone˺ knows best who has strayed from His Way and who is ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.explanation: Once you have called and debated with wisdom, clear proofs, and kindness, leave their final accounting to God, for your Lord alone knows best who has stubbornly strayed from His path and who is open-hearted and rightly guided to the truth and He will repay each person according to their deeds.

phrases.translation: If you retaliate, then let it be equivalent to what you have suffered.
phrases.explanation: If you believers retaliate against someone who has wronged you, you may punish only in the exact measure of the wrong inflicted upon you without exceeding the limit. Early reports state this was revealed at Uhud when Muslims vowed to mutilate the enemy in retaliation for the mutilation of Hamzah.

phrases.translation: But if you patiently endure, it is certainly best for those who are patient
phrases.explanation: Yet if you restrain yourselves from taking revenge, endure the wrong patiently for the sake of God, and leave the matter to Him, patient endurance is far better and more richly rewarded by God in both worlds for those who are steadfast and seek the reward of God rather than personal vengeance.

phrases.translation: Be patient ˹O Prophet˺, for your patience is only with Allah’s help.
phrases.explanation: Therefore be patient, O Prophet, in bearing the harm and insults of your enemies for the sake of God, and know that your ability to be patient comes only through God’s help, grace, and enabling support in every trial you face as you convey the message of your Lord to humanity.

phrases.translation: Do not grieve over those ˹who disbelieve˺, nor be distressed by their schemes
phrases.explanation: Do not grieve over the disbelievers when they reject your sincere counsel and turn away from faith, nor let your chest tighten with distress over the plots and slanders they devise against you, for God will protect you and grant you victory over all who oppose His truth and mock His revelation.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is with those who shun evil and who do good ˹deeds˺
phrases.explanation: Surely God is with those who fear Him by avoiding what He has forbidden and who do good by fulfilling His obligatory duties and commands with excellence, supporting them at all times with His protection, victory, guidance, and unfailing mercy in this world and on the Day of Resurrection.
